result:
F-DG3-100 is repaired and the changes are left uncommitted in `/home/user/wt/dg3-kbe-f` for you to integrate. All six acceptance checks passed. One `pnpm test` combination (Node 22, `C.UTF-8`) needed a second run because of an unrelated web test failure, described below. The DG2 historical validator passed (exit 0) before I started and again at the end. Time: 13:41:31 to 14:10:47 UTC.

**The repair**
- **An exercised `EvalError` now fails (choice (a)).** The four error catches in the engine now let `EvalError` through instead of turning it into an `internal` problem: `validateFormula`, `evaluateFormula`, the tree walk in `evaluateAst`, and `formatDecimal` in `value.ts`. The error escapes, so every test that reaches the path fails, whatever that test checks. Option (b) only protects tests that call its helper.
- **Production behaviour:** any other unexpected error is still a 422 `formula.syntax` `internal` problem (or null from `formatDecimal`); tests in both projects pin this. An `EvalError` can't occur in production. If it ever did, the API would answer 500 `internal`, not show it as a user syntax error.
- **Internal failures fail the tests.** `checkOutcome`, the payload test and every row of the rejection table now refuse `reason: "internal"`. No existing input produced one, so there was nothing to stop and report.
- **Regression test:** 4 tests in the no-codegen project generate code inside each of the four catches and require the `EvalError` to come out.
- **The whole import closure is guarded.** `value.ts` gets every engine-source lint rule, with an import allowlist of `decimal.js` only. It needed no exception. It is also in the scan's file set.
- **Closure test:** it computes the static import closure from `formula/index.ts` and asserts that every file in it is covered by the lint rules and the scan. Three deliberate mutations each made it fail.
- **The record:** ADR-0024 §6 is corrected on all four points, and `p3-work-split.md` §9 has a new round-4 heading with item 26.

**Which layer refuses each form** (reviewer's probes, unedited copies, in disposable clones)

| Form | Refused by |
|---|---|
| S1 (`tokenize.ts` code generation, exercised by fuzz and 'été') | run time (passed all layers in round 3) |
| S2 | run time |
| S3 (code generation when `m = 50`) | run time (passed all layers in round 3) |
| V1 (`node:vm` in `value.ts`) | lint and scan (passed all layers in round 3) |
| V2 (`new Function` in `value.ts`) | lint, scan and run time |

- The 18 earlier forms (O1–O6, N1–N12) are all still refused by both lint and scan.
- With S1 and S3 applied, the exercised probe now fails (vitest exit 1).
- I also ran a check that is not the delivered code: with the rethrow deleted, the internal-failure rule alone still fails the fuzz tests for S1 and S3.

**Test counts**
- **`pnpm test`:** exit 0 on Node 24 and Node 22, with the locale unset and with `C.UTF-8`. The first invocation ran 1593 tests (baseline 1587); the no-codegen invocation had 199 passed and 1 skipped out of 200 (baseline 190).
- **Integration:** 793 of 793 passed on a disposable PostgreSQL, port 23100 (same as the baseline).
- **typecheck, build, lint, the engine eslint run and prettier:** all exit 0.

**Things to know**
- **One skipped test:** the lint-coverage test runs only in the normal unit project. ESLint itself generates code from strings (through ajv), so it can't run under the no-codegen flag. The closure and scan-coverage test runs in both projects.
- **Failed run:** on the first Node 22 `C.UTF-8` run, one web test failed: `session-identity.test.tsx` (F-DG2-500 sign-out). The same command then passed, and the same test appears in earlier failed logs from other tasks. I didn't investigate it because it's outside my scope. Both logs are kept.
- **What remains open, as the ADR says:** `decimal.js` is outside the lint and scan checks (it contains no `eval(` or `Function(` calls). A run-time-assembled key on a path no test exercises (the Q1–Q5 style) still gets past both static checks.
- **Setup:** `pnpm install --offline` failed because the pnpm store is read-only in this sandbox, so the clones got their `node_modules` copied from the worktree.
- **Blocked command:** a safety check stopped a command that would have deleted empty `.cc-writes` folders; nothing ran. A listing then found no such folders in the source directories, so nothing needed removing.
- **Untracked files:** some top-level dotfiles (`.bashrc`, `.idea`, …) were already untracked in the worktree before I started. They aren't mine and shouldn't be integrated.

Files are in `docs/delivery/handbacks/DG3/`:
- `T-DG3-KBE-F-kpi-benefits-engineer.md`
- `T-DG3-KBE-F-evidence/` (logs and the diff)
